pr_title: Unify reading from procfs to get network related information
pr_body:
This PR makes sure undocumented exceptions like `UnauthorizedAccessException` does not bubble to user code when querying network interface information.

We will throw `NetworkInformationException` with the message "An error was encountered while querying information from the operating system." and pass the inner exception along. It seems more appropriate than `PlatformNotSupportedException` (which is currently thrown when the files do not exist).

Fixes #62513

Issue Details
This PR makes sure undocumented exceptions like `UnauthorizedAccessException` does not bubble to user code when querying network interface information. I am still a bit unsure whether using `PlatformNotSupportedException` is the right direction here since we generally throw that one for platforms like Android where there is no OS API to retrieve the information, (whereas restricted container just is not allowed to read the information). Another candidate would be `NetworkInformationException` with a default (0) `ErrorCode`. Opinions welcome. fixes #22927

issue_context.title: [Linux] procfs file reads and UnauthorizedAccessException handling
issue_context.body:
In restricted environments such as a container with limited access, shared hosting, chroot and other forms of sandbox, .NET process may not have read permissions on procfs files, while the file may exist. This can lead to `UnauthorizedAccessException`.

While most of the managed code reading procfs files in the runtime repo found by `git grep /proc ':/*.cs' ':/!*[tT]est*'` seem to handle unauhorized access case, we should try to make the user-experience consistent and align varied styles where possible. A few examples:

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/c8ede5c4b1aba85fc894d5faed42d6d5186eabe1/src/libraries/System.Net.NetworkInformation/src/System/Net/NetworkInformation/LinuxNetworkInterface.cs#L38

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/c8ede5c4b1aba85fc894d5faed42d6d5186eabe1/src/libraries/Common/src/Interop/Linux/procfs/Interop.ProcFsStat.TryReadStatusFile.cs#L149

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/c8ede5c4b1aba85fc894d5faed42d6d5186eabe1/src/libraries/Common/src/Interop/Linux/procfs/Interop.ProcFsStat.ParseMapModules.cs#L26-L27

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/c8ede5c4b1aba85fc894d5faed42d6d5186eabe1/src/libraries/System.Net.NetworkInformation/src/System/Net/NetworkInformation/StringParsingHelpers.Connections.cs#L36

and then there are cases in `NetworkInformation`, which do not handle the exception at all. Majority of procfs files listed in `NetworkInformation/NetworkFiles.cs` are read via `StringParsingHelpers`. Some call sites catch `IOException` and `UnauthorizedAccessException`, others don't and it seems unintentional. For instance, [`GetIcmpV4Statistics`](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.net.networkinformation.ipglobalproperties.geticmpv4statistics?view=net-6.0) and [`GetTcpIPv4Statistics`](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.net.networkinformation.ipglobalproperties.gettcpipv4statistics?view=net-6.0) docs do not mention `PlatformNotSupportedException`, `IOException` or `UnauthorizedAccessException` are the possible exceptions which these APIs can throw, only `NetworkInformationException` is noted.

this would be nice to fix for consistency.
Triage: It would be nice clean up. Should not be that difficult to do.

review_comments: it may be worth of putting in at least some text - in case we ever need to do some troubleshooting.
both constructors taking message are internal (thus inaccessible to the unit tests). We could subclass it, but that does not seem worth the gain

This may be out of scope for this but the old (and new) behavior seem. wrong to me.
Let say the kernel was built without IPv6 support (or v4 in distant future). The file would be missing and we would always throw even if there is nothing wrong.

In many cases like this it feels it would be better to return empty collection. Since the networking grabs massive amount of information had several cases in the past when we thrown on stupid things even if the caller really does not care.
I know this is existing code but loading everything to memory just to sound lines seems quite inefficient. We may not care for routes (in most cases) but this may be good candidate for mmap.
or maybe StreamReader reading into a `Span<char>`
Why are we getting rid of the file existence checks?

The reason was to change the type of exception thrown to something more appropriate. PNSE is not mentioned by the docs and feels more appropriate for cases when there is no (implemented?) way of accessing the information in question.

Omitting the file existence checks will still make the code throw, but it will throw `NetworkInformationException` instead (which is mentioned in the docs), and its inner exception will provide more info to the user.

Changing the exception type is technically breaking change. But same argument as above could be applicable here. It feels it would be better and perhaps make the helper nullable and deal with lack of the file more gracefully.
